title: 「内密出産」タブー視を越えられるか　病院先行、政治に支援の動き
extracted_text:
女性が病院以外に身元を明かさず出産する「内密出産」を巡り、熊本の病院が受け入れを始めてから6年がたった。東京の病院が続き、大阪府泉佐野市も2026年度中の導入をめざす。民間や地方自治体の取り組みが先行するなか、内密出産をタブー視していた政治も動きだした。

4月6日、熊本市の慈恵病院。3月に始動した自民党の「内密出産」について考えるプロジェクトチーム（PT）のメンバーが訪れた。座長の松野博一元官房長官と坂本哲志元孤独・孤立対策相、党特命委員長の阿部俊子氏だ。

慈恵病院は19年、病院以外で産む「孤立出産」を防ぐため全国で初めて内密出産の受け入れを発表した。松野氏らは07年に設置された「こうのとりのゆりかご」（赤ちゃんポスト）に最初に預けられた宮津航一さんや熊本市の大西一史市長とも意見交換した。

松野氏は4月14日のPTで「一歩ずつでも前に進める」と意欲を示した。

内密出産は慈恵病院に続き、25年に東京都墨田区の賛育会病院が受け入れを始めた。泉佐野市は26年度中に「りんくう総合医療センター」で運用を始める予定だ。

慈恵病院では21年12月〜26年4月下旬に69人の乳児が生まれたという。このうち15人は逆子だったり、心拍状態が悪化したりして帝王切開で誕生した。25年12月の参院予算委員会に参考人として出席した蓮田健院長は帝王切開の事例に関し「もし自宅で出産したら赤ちゃんは亡くなっていたのではないかという事例があった」と説明した。

内密出産を望む女性は親など周囲に頼れず、孤立する女性が大半だ。厳しい家庭・経済環境におかれた人も多い。

内密出産を規定する法律はない。厚生労働省と法務省は22年9月、慈恵病院や熊本市などの要請を受けて初のガイドラインを策定した。病院側に女性の身元情報の保存を求め、地方自治体が戸籍を作成できるなどと明示した。

一方、ガイドラインでは内密出産を「推奨するものではない」と記し、政府の立場も強調した。「育児放棄を助長する」などといった批判があることに配慮したとみられる。政府・自民党で議論が進まなかった背景がうかがえる表現だ。

18年から国会で政府に対応を求めてきた国民民主党の伊藤孝恵参院議員は政治のタブー視について「保守的な家族観や倫理観がある」と推測する。「国会で最初に取り上げた当時は『国が壊れてしまう』などと批判もたくさん受けた」と明かす。

ガイドラインをつくっても解決できない課題は多い。①出自を知る権利の担保②病院の負担軽減③出自を知る権利と女性の匿名性の両立――といった点が指摘される。

慈恵病院では出産や滞在にかかる費用を病院側で負担している。民間の病院は倒産する可能性もある。個人情報である出生に関わる情報を民間病院が長期にわたって管理するのは適切ではないとの見方は根強い。

伊藤氏はこのほど内密出産に関する法案の骨子案をまとめた。拠点となる病院の確保や病院への支援、出自を知る権利を担保する制度の構築、子の養育環境の整備といった国の役割を規定する内容だ。これからも政府・与党に法制化を働きかけていくと話す。

とはいえ政府は慎重な姿勢を崩していない。高市早苗首相は4月7日の参院予算委員会で「様々な意見がある。慎重な議論が必要だ」と語るにとどめた。

他国はどうか。韓国では23年、病院の出産記録があるにもかかわらず出生届がない「消えた赤ちゃん」が8年間で2000人以上にのぼることが判明した。政府が法制化に動き、24年7月に「保護（内密）出産」制度が始まった。

ドイツも14年に内密出産に関する法律を施行した。

賛育会病院の賀藤均院長は4月15日、超党派の「児童の養護と未来を考える議員連盟」に出席し、法制化を求めた。内密出産の制度を整えた他国の例を挙げて「新生児の遺棄や殺人、赤ちゃんポストへの預け入れを激減させる可能性がある」と説明した。

菅義偉政権で初代の孤独・孤立対策相を務め、自民党の「内密出産」について考えるプロジェクトチーム（PT）の設置を主導した坂本哲志衆院議員（熊本3区）に話を聞いた。

◇

――PT設置の経緯は。

「担当相として様々な世代の孤立に向き合った。若い女性が予期せぬ妊娠に悩み、孤独を感じる問題が頭にあった。昨年、私が党の孤独・孤立対策特命委員会の委員長に就き、PTをつくろうとなった」

――慈恵病院などは国の支援や法制化を求めています。

「議論は続けるが、法制化までは相当の距離がある。まず国ができることを考えたい。熊本市のように自治体が相談窓口を設けるような取り組みを支援できないか。子どもの出自の情報を公的に保管する方策はあるか。政府が6月ごろに策定する『経済財政運営と改革の基本方針（骨太の方針）』に入るように努力したい」

「内密出産は健診なしの出産の可能性もあるため、母体のリスクも伴う。行政の相談窓口と医療側との新たな連携関係も求められる」

――保守的な家族観を持つ人には育児放棄につながるといった懸念もあります。

「慈恵病院が赤ちゃんポストを始めた時、地元に賛否両論があったのは事実だ。だが、内密出産の開始時は『なんとかしないと』という雰囲気ができていたように感じる。自宅などで産む孤立出産は危険だ。少子化が進む中で、子どもの遺棄や殺害事例も相次ぐ。市民に危機感と理解が広がった。慈恵病院と熊本市の成果の1つだ」

「生まれた子どもに罪はなく、放っておけない。確かに保守的な考え方の人の懸念もあるが、社会が一定の責任を果たすことが必要だと理解してもらえるのではないか。党も考える時期に来たということだと思う」

自民党のある議員に、なぜ内密出産への関心が高まらず、法制化が進まないのかと聞いたことがある。答えは単純明快。「票にならないから」だった。

確かに内密出産を必要とする女性の数は多くない。法制化が実現しても、選挙前に成果として訴えることは難しいかもしれない。だが、声なき声に耳を傾け、困難な状況にある人に手を差し伸べる社会をつくるのが政治の役割でもある。

こども家庭庁によると、心中以外の虐待で死亡した0歳児の半数近くは、出生したその日に命を落としている。医師が立ち会わない孤立出産のケースが大半とみられる。政府は少子化への対策にも取り組んでいる。病院の篤志にいつまでも頼ってはいられない。与野党で議論が加速することを心から期待したい。（山内菜穂子）

【関連記事】
translated_text:
Six years have passed since a hospital in Kumamoto began accepting "confidential births," where women give birth at hospitals without revealing their identity to anyone other than the facility. A hospital in Tokyo followed, and Izumisano City in Osaka Prefecture aims to introduce the system during fiscal year 2026. While private and local government initiatives have taken the lead, politics—which had viewed confidential birth as a taboo—is also starting to move.

On April 6, at Jikei Hospital in Kumamoto City. Members of the Liberal Democratic Party's project team (PT) on confidential birth, which launched in March, visited. They were party chair Hiroshi Matsuno, former chief cabinet secretary, former minister for loneliness and social isolation Tesshi Sakamoto, and chair of the party's special mission committee Toshiko Abe.

In 2019, Jikei Hospital became the first in Japan to announce acceptance of confidential births to prevent "isolated births"—women giving birth outside hospitals. The group also exchanged views with Koichi Miyazu, the first infant placed in the "stork's cradle" (baby hatch) established in 2007, and Kumamoto City Mayor Kazufumi Ohnishi.

At the PT meeting on April 14, Matsuno expressed enthusiasm, saying, "We want to move forward one step at a time."

Following Jikei Hospital, Tokyo's Sankaikai Hospital in Sumida Ward began accepting confidential births in 2025. Izumisako City plans to operate the system at Rinku General Medical Center during fiscal year 2026.

At Jikei Hospital, 69 infants were born between December 2021 and late April 2026. Of these, 15 were delivered by cesarean section due to breech presentation or worsening fetal heart conditions. At the House of Councillors Budget Committee in December 2025, Director Ken莲田健 (rensheng) explained that among the cesarean cases, "there were instances where the baby might have died if born at home."

Most women seeking confidential births are those who cannot rely on their parents or others around them and end up isolated. Many also face difficult family or economic circumstances.

There is no law regulating confidential births. In September 2022, the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare and the Ministry of Justice, responding to requests from Jikei Hospital and Kumamoto City, formulated the first guidelines. These require hospitals to store women's identity information and allow local governments to create family registers.

However, the guidelines state that confidential births are "not recommended," emphasizing the government's position. This appears to take into account criticism that the system could encourage child abandonment. The expression suggests why discussion stalled in the government and LDP.

Since 2018, National Democratic Party member of the House of Councillors Tomoe Ito has been urging the government to act in the Diet. Regarding the political taboo, she speculates, "There are conservative views on family and ethics." She reveals, "When I first raised this in the Diet, there was much criticism, including that 'the country would collapse.'"

Even with guidelines, many challenges remain: ensuring the right to know one's origin, reducing the burden on hospitals, and balancing the right to know one's origin with women's anonymity.

Jikei Hospital covers the costs of births and stays. Private hospitals could go bankrupt. There is a persistent view that it is inappropriate for private hospitals to long-term manage personal information related to births.

Recently, Ito compiled a draft outline for a law on confidential birth. It would define the national role of securing base hospitals, supporting hospitals, building systems to ensure the right to know one's origin, and improving child-rearing environments. She says she will continue pushing the government and ruling party for legislation.

However, the government remains cautious. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said at the House of Councils Budget Committee on April 7, "There are various opinions. Careful discussion is necessary."

What about other countries? In South Korea, in 2023, over 2,000 "disappeared babies"—children for whom birth registration was not filed despite hospital birth records—were identified over eight years. The government moved to enact legislation, and a "protected (confidential) birth" system began in July 2024.

Germany also enacted a law on confidential birth in 2014.

On April 15, Sankaikai Hospital Director Hitoshi Kaito attended the cross-party Diet member alliance for child welfare and the future, calling for legislation. Citing examples of other countries that have established confidential birth systems, he explained that it "could significantly reduce infant abandonment, infanticide, and placements in baby hatches."

We spoke with Representative Tesshi Sakamoto (Kumamoto District 3), who served as the first minister for loneliness and social isolation under the Suga administration and led the establishment of the LDP's project team on confidential birth.

---

 What was the background of the PT's establishment?

"As minister, I faced isolation across various generations. The issue that weighed on my mind was young women facing unexpected pregnancies and feeling alone. Last year, I became chair of the party's special committee on loneliness and social isolation, and the PT was established."

 Jikei Hospital and others are requesting national support and legislation.

"We will continue discussion, but there's considerable distance to legislation. I want to consider what the nation can do first. Isn't it possible to support initiatives like Kumamoto City setting up consultation windows? Is there a way for the government to publicly store children's origin information? I'll work to get it into the government's 'Basic Economic and Fiscal Policy Directions' (骨太の方針) planned for around June."

"Confidential births may occur without prenatal checkups, so there are also risks to mothers. New coordination between administrative consultation windows and medical providers is also required."

"There are also concerns among those with conservative family values that it could lead to child abandonment."

"When Jikei Hospital started the baby hatch, there were indeed pro and con voices in the community. But I feel that at the time confidential birth started, there was a sense that 'we have to do something.' Isolated births at home are dangerous. With the declining birth rate, cases of child abandonment and killings have also increased. Crisis awareness and understanding have spread among citizens. One of the achievements of Jikei Hospital and Kumamoto City."

"Children who are born are not guilty and cannot be left alone. There are indeed concerns from those with conservative views, but I hope they can understand that society needs to take a certain level of responsibility. I think the party has also come to a time to consider this."

We asked an LDP member why there hasn't been more interest in confidential birth and why legislation hasn't advanced. The answer was simple and clear: "Because it doesn't win votes."

Indeed, the number of women who need confidential birth isn't large. Even if legislation passes, it may be difficult to claim as an achievement before an election. However, listening to voiceless voices and creating a society that reaches out to those in difficult situations is also the role of politics.

According to the Children and Families Agency, nearly half of infants who die from abuse (excluding suicide) lose their lives on the day they are born. Most appear to be cases of isolated births without medical attendance. The government is also addressing the declining birth rate. We cannot rely indefinitely on hospitals' dedication. I sincerely hope discussion accelerates across both ruling and opposition parties.

[Additional coverage]
title_en: Can Confidential Birth Move Beyond Taboo? Hospitals Lead as Politics Follows Support
